title: Dilatation at one residue point lowers the index-one differential defect
statement:
Let $R\hookrightarrow A$ be an injective local homomorphism of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$, assume $\mathfrak m_A=\pi A$, and assume the residue-field extension $\kappa(A)/\kappa(R)$ is separable, allowing transcendental extensions [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Let $B$ be a commutative finite-type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] on which multiplication by $\pi$ is injective. Assume $\operatorname{Spec}(B[1/\pi])$ is smooth over $\operatorname{Frac}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\varphi:B\to A$ be an $R$-algebra homomorphism. Put
$$M_B(\varphi)=A\otimes_{B,\varphi}\Omega_{B/R},\qquad T_B(\varphi)=\{m\in M_B(\varphi):am=0\text{ for some }0\ne a\in A\},$$
using Kähler differentials and tensor products [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and put $\delta_B(\varphi)=\operatorname{length}_A T_B(\varphi)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Set
$$I=\ker(B\xrightarrow{\varphi}A\to\kappa(A)),\qquad B'=B[I/\pi]\subset B[1/\pi],$$
where $B[I/\pi]$ is the $B$-subalgebra generated by $b/\pi$ for all $b\in I$. Then $B'$ is a finite-type $R$-algebra, multiplication by $\pi$ on $B'$ is injective, and the inclusion induces $B'[1/\pi]=B[1/\pi]$. The homomorphism $B[1/\pi]\to\operatorname{Frac}A$ extending $\varphi$ restricts to an $R$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi':B'\to A$, necessarily given by $\varphi'(b/\pi)=\varphi(b)/\pi$. For $M_{B'}(\varphi')$, $T_{B'}(\varphi')$ and $\delta_{B'}(\varphi')$ defined by the same displayed formulas with $B',\varphi'$ replacing $B,\varphi$, the torsion length is finite and
$$\delta_{B'}(\varphi')\leq\max\{0,\delta_B(\varphi)-1\}.$$
No excellence, completeness or separability of the fraction-field extension is required.

source.place: BLR 3.6 Proposition 3 and its proof, printed p.79 (PDF p.85); affine dilatation construction preceding 3.2 Proposition 1, and Proposition 1(a)–(b), printed p.63 (PDF p.69) Primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. proof.text: A DVR is Noetherian since every ideal is principal [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Thus $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Choose ideal generators $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $I$. Then $B'=B[b_1/\pi,\ldots,b_s/\pi]$, because $b=\sum c_i b_i$ gives $b/\pi=\sum c_i(b_i/\pi)$. This proves finite type. The injectivity of multiplication by $\pi$ on $B$ embeds $B$ in $B[1/\pi]$; hence the same multiplication is injective on its subalgebra $B'$, and $B'[1/\pi]=B[1/\pi]$. Since $\varphi(I)\subseteq\pi A$, the map to $\operatorname{Frac}A$ sends every generator $b_i/\pi$ into $A$. Its restriction is the asserted $\varphi'$, and the formula and uniqueness follow from $\pi(b_i/\pi)=b_i$ and cancellation in $A$.

source.place: 3.2 affine dilatation construction and Proposition 1(a)-(b), printed pp.62-63 (PDF pp.68-69).

proof.text: Put $k=R/\pi R$, $D=B/I$, and $Q=D\otimes_B\Omega_{B/R}$. The map $D\hookrightarrow\kappa(A)$ is injective, so $D$ is a nonzero finite-type $k$-domain. Its fraction field is a finitely generated intermediate field of $\kappa(A)/k$, and is separable over $k$ by [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: every finitely generated subfield of this fraction field is also one of $\kappa(A)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-generic-point-over-field] to $D/k$. Also $D$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $Q$ is finite: if $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ generate $B/R$, the $dx_i$ generate $\Omega_{B/R}$ by the Leibniz rule. Apply [lem-pur-noetherian-algebra-module-generic-freeness] with base ring and algebra both $D$, and module $Q$. Multiplying the two nonzero localization elements gives $g\ne0$ with $D_g$ smooth over $k$ and $Q_g$ free of finite rank. Freeness remains after a further localization by localizing a basis; smoothness on a smaller principal open follows from its local definition. The free rank is finite because $Q_g$ is finitely generated.

source.place: 3.6 Proposition 3 proof, printed p.79 (PDF p.85), smoothness at the generic point of the residue closure; 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed p.68 (PDF p.74), free restriction. Supporting Stacks 07ND (algebra-lemma-smooth-at-generic-point), 051R (algebra-lemma-generic-flatness-Noetherian).

proof.text: Lift $g$ to $f\in B$. Since $f\notin I$, $\varphi(f)$ is a unit in $A$. We may replace $B$ by $B_f$: the kernel of $B_f\to\kappa(A)$ is $I B_f$, and its dilatation is exactly $B'_f$, since its generators are $b/(f^a\pi)$ with $b\in I$. Both evaluation maps factor through these localizations, and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identifies their evaluated differential modules with the original ones. Now $Y=\operatorname{Spec}D_g$ is smooth over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], and $\Omega^1_{X/R}|_Y$ is finite free for $X=\operatorname{Spec}B_f$ by [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]: restriction along $Y\hookrightarrow X$ corresponds to $D_g\otimes_{B_f}\Omega_{B_f/R}=Q_g$, and a finite basis gives a free associated sheaf on each principal open. Apply [lem-sfb-adapted-smooth-ambient] at the generic point of $Y$, the image of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. It gives, after a further affine restriction, $X=\operatorname{Spec}E\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}C$, $E=C/H$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$, $J=(\pi,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$, and an etale coordinate system $y_1,\ldots,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_n$. The differential map on $Y$ is an isomorphism and $C$ is Noetherian. Every such open contains the whole valued point: its inverse image is an open containing the closed point of a local spectrum. Its ring map $C/J\to\kappa(A)$ remains injective, since it is a restriction to a nonempty open of the integral residue closure. These affine restrictions preserve the evaluated modules by the same localization lemma: if $V=\operatorname{Spec}E$ is not principal in $X$, choose a principal open $D(f')\subseteq V$ of $X$ containing the point, so $\varphi(f')\in A^\times$, $E_{f'}=(B_f)_{f'}$, and both rings and their dilatations are compared through this common localization.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed pp.68-69 (PDF pp.74-75), applied at the generic residue point as in 3.6 Proposition 3, p.79. Algebraic localization and restriction details supplied explicitly.

proof.text: We have $H\subseteq J^2$. Indeed for $h\in H$ write $h=\pi c+\sum_j z_jc_j$. By the isomorphism and differential basis supplied by [lem-sfb-adapted-smooth-ambient], reduction of $dh$ modulo $J$ is zero and hence every $c_j\in J$. Thus $h=\pi c+u$ with $u\in J^2$. Under the evaluation $C\to E\to A$, $J$ maps into $\pi A$ and $h$ maps to zero. It follows that $\pi c$ maps into $\pi^2 A$, so $c$ maps into $\pi A$. Injectivity of $C/J\to\kappa(A)$ now gives $c\in J$. Therefore $h\in J^2$. This uses the single generic residue point in place of the family in condition (N) of BLR 3.3.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, key calculation on printed p.69 (PDF p.75); 3.6 Proposition 3, replacing schematic density by injective evaluation at the generic residue point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-centre-dilatation-coordinates] to $C,J$. Write $C'=C[J/\pi]$, $z'_j=z_j/\pi$. It is Noetherian, $\pi$-torsion-free, and its differential basis is $dy_i,dz'_j$, with $dz_j=\pi dz'_j$ and $C'[1/\pi]=C[1/\pi]$. Let $H'=\{c'\in C':\pi^a c'\in HC'\text{ for some }a\ge0\}$. The image of $C'\to E[1/\pi]$ is $E[(J/H)/\pi]$, exactly the local dilatation from step 1. Its kernel is $H'$: being zero after localization means precisely being killed by a power of $\pi$ modulo $HC'$. Thus the dilatation algebra here is $E'=C'/H'$. Evaluation $C'\to A$, $z'_j\mapsto\varphi(z_j)/\pi$, kills $H'$ by cancellation in $A$. For $h\in H\subseteq J^2$, $h^\sharp=h/\pi^2\in C'$ since $JC'\subseteq\pi C'$, and $h^\sharp\in H'$.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed p.70 (PDF p.76), ambient dilatation and saturated defining ideal; 3.2 affine construction.

proof.text: For $h\in H$, write $dh=\sum b_i\,dy_i+\sum c_j\,dz_j$ in $C$ and $dh^\sharp=\sum b_i^\sharp\,dy_i+\sum c_j^\sharp\,dz'_j$ in $C'$. Differentiating $h=\pi^2h^\sharp$ and using [lem-sfb-smooth-centre-dilatation-coordinates], the basis coefficients satisfy $b_i=\pi^2b_i^\sharp$ and $c_j=\pi c_j^\sharp$; cancellation is permitted because $\pi$ is injective on $C'$. Evaluating at the lifted point therefore divides the $y$ columns of the relation row for $h$ by $\pi^2$ and its $z$ columns by $\pi$.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed p.70 (PDF p.76), differential coefficient equations.

proof.text: Choose finite generators $h_1,\ldots,h_s$ of $H$ and $u_1,\ldots,u_t$ of $H'$; $C$ and $C'$ are Noetherian in the two coordinate nodes [lem-sfb-adapted-smooth-ambient, lem-sfb-smooth-centre-dilatation-coordinates]. By [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps], $\Omega_{E/R}$ and $\Omega_{E'/R}$ are quotients of the respective ambient free differential modules by the rows $dh_\lambda$ and $du_\mu$. Tensoring these quotients with $A$ gives the corresponding quotients by evaluated rows: a bilinear map from a quotient is exactly a bilinear map killing the relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus the modules in question are $A^N/L$ and $A^N/L'$, $N=r+n$, with these row submodules. Any $du$, $u\in H'$, gives a row in $L'$: writing $u=\sum a_\mu u_\mu$, differentiating, and evaluating kills every $u_\mu da_\mu$ term. In particular all $dh_\lambda^\sharp$ are relation rows in $L'$.

source.place: 3.3 Lemma 2 presentation argument, printed p.66 (PDF p.72), and Proposition 5 proof p.70; quotient differential exact sequence, Stacks 00RU (algebra-lemma-differential-seq).

proof.text: Let $F=\operatorname{Frac}A$. The row spans of $L,L'$ in $F^N$ have the same dimension $q$. In fact $H'[1/\pi]=H[1/\pi]$ inside $C'[1/\pi]=C[1/\pi]$ [lem-sfb-smooth-centre-dilatation-coordinates and step 5]. Each generator of either localized ideal is a finite sum of multiples of generators of the other. Differentiating such a sum and evaluating in $F$ kills the terms involving the generators themselves. Hence the two relation spans agree under the invertible diagonal change of basis $dy_i\mapsto dy_i$, $dz_j\mapsto\pi dz'_j$. This also covers $q=0$, without an equidimensionality assertion about the generic fibre.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, Jacobian ranks, printed pp.70-71 (PDF pp.76-77); explicit ideal-localization argument.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-relation-minors-length] to the finite generating matrices of $L,L'$. It proves both torsion lengths finite. If $q>0$, choose a $q$-minor $\Delta$ of the evaluated rows $dh_\lambda$ attaining $v(\Delta)=\delta_B(\varphi)$, where $v(\pi)=1$ since $\mathfrak m_A=\pi A$. Take the corresponding minor $\Delta^\sharp$ of the rows $dh_\lambda^\sharp$. If $p$ of its columns are $y$ columns, step 6 gives $\Delta^\sharp=\pi^{-(q+p)}\Delta$. Add those relation rows to the generating matrix of $L'$; its quotient and rank do not change. The same minors formula gives
$$\delta_{B'}(\varphi')\le v(\Delta^\sharp)=\delta_B(\varphi)-q-p\le\delta_B(\varphi)-1.$$
All its entries are in $A$, so the finite valuation on the right is nonnegative; in particular this case forces $\delta_B(\varphi)\ge1$. If $q=0$, both row submodules vanish, because $A^N\hookrightarrow F^N$ is injective. Both evaluated modules are free and both torsion lengths are zero. Together these cases give the asserted maximum. Steps 2-3 identified these local evaluated modules with the original ones, so the bound holds for the original $B,B'$.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed pp.70-71 (PDF pp.76-77), minor scaling; 3.6 Proposition 3, printed p.79 (PDF p.85). Zero row-rank case proved directly.
